subject: physics

moments.title: Stefan's experimental law
moments.body: Stefan, examining experimental data, finds that total radiated power from a hot body scales as T^4. He uses the law to make the first reasonable estimate of the Sun's surface temperature (~5,700 K).
moments.takeaway: A T^4 law from experimental data alone.

moments.title: Boltzmann's thermodynamic derivation
moments.body: Boltzmann derives Stefan's law from classical thermodynamics — treating radiation as a gas with pressure P = u/3. The Stefan-Boltzmann law sigma T^4 is born.
moments.takeaway: A theoretical derivation backs up Stefan's empirical law.

moments.title: Wien's displacement law
moments.body: Wien shows the peak wavelength of blackbody radiation scales as 1/T. Hotter objects peak at shorter wavelengths. He wins the 1911 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Hotter is bluer. Wien's law lets us measure stellar temperatures from colour.

moments.title: Planck completes the picture
moments.body: Planck's quantum derivation of the blackbody curve subsumes both Stefan-Boltzmann and Wien as limiting cases. Classical thermodynamics is succeeded by quantum statistical mechanics.
moments.takeaway: Stefan, Boltzmann and Wien all follow from Planck's quantum hypothesis.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Stefan-Boltzmann is central to climate models, stellar astrophysics, and thermal imaging. Earth's effective temperature (255 K) is too cold for liquid water without the greenhouse effect.
now.open_questions: How do clouds and aerosols modify Earth's effective radiating temperature?

reflection: Stefan derived a law from data alone. Planck derived it from a deep principle. Which kind of derivation is more 'scientific'?
